pdf_note: J-STAGE open access PDF; the figure is an embedded raster image of about 220 ppi

x_axis.note: vertical grid lines at slope 10 and 25 deg (frame at 0 and 30 deg agrees, 15.78 px per deg)

y_axis.note: horizontal grid lines at slip ratio 0.1 and 0.9 (grid lines at 0.2, 0.5, 0.6 and the frame at 0 and 1 agree, 413 px per unit)

marker.identification: manual: one seed per nominal slope at the purple triangle marker of b10 (legend), refined to the centroid of that colour

meta.source_title: Effects of wheel width on running performance of four-wheeled small lunar rover (Watanabe, Maru, Kawaguchi, Tanaka; Transactions of the JSME, in Japanese, Vol. 92, No. 956, 2026)
meta.evidence_row: TM3-047; TM3-048; TM3-049 (same source, other findings)
meta.vehicle: four wheeled small lunar rover, 3D printed ABS, 1.5 kg (ballasted to the same mass for every wheel set), wheelbase 200 mm, all wheels driven at 10 rpm
meta.grousers: 12 lugs, 10 mm high, 3 mm thick, equally spaced
meta.soil: FJS-1 lunar regolith simulant, about 110 mm deep
meta.preparation: tilting simulant bed 2000 mm by 1000 mm, electric lift up to 37 deg; soil tilled from depth and levelled before each run; mean of 9 inclinometer readings on the course within 1 deg of the target; vane shear torque at 20 mm depth below 0.30 cNm
meta.comparability_note: Each point is the mean of 5 runs over 700 mm (error bars 1 SD, not transcribed). Slip ratio by Eq. (1): 1 minus V over r omega when driving, with r the radius including lugs. x is the nominal slope set for the test; the text states the mean of 9 readings on the course was within 1 deg of it, so x_unc is 1 deg. y read from the marker of this wheel width, refined to the centroid of its colour; markers of the seven widths overlap at low slopes, so partly hidden markers were kept only when roughly half or more of the marker was visible, and fully hidden ones are left out (10 and 15 deg markers hidden; the rover stuck at 30 deg (text, Sec. 3.1), so no marker at 30 deg). Partial hiding can shift a centroid by up to the marker radius, which is the stated y_unc. load_per_wheel_N derived here as 1.5 kg times 9.81 divided by 4 wheels. Very light rover (1.5 kg) with narrow 3D printed wheels; the paper scales a 5 to 10 kg lunar rover to 1/6 mass, not to Earth sand traverses.
